speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my examination. I see you are a newborn presenting with a generalized rash; to better understand this, could you please describe when the rash first appeared and if it seems to worsen at any specific time of day?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the rash accompanied by any fever, poor feeding, or difficulty breathing? Additionally, have you noticed if the rash has a specific pattern, such as scaling, pustules, or blisters?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the sparing of the palms and soles combined with pustules on an erythematous base is very telling. Given the mother's history of untreated gonorrhea, do the baby have any signs of sepsis such as lethargy or temperature instability? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and Blood Culture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Sepsis with Disseminated Gonococcal Infection.
